title: Malformed MQTT and counter records can terminate the server
summary:
### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

NATS Server decodes stored MQTT state and JetStream responses, and can maintain counters sourced from other streams.

### Problem Description

Several decoding paths did not safely handle missing or null fields. Malformed MQTT state, internal responses or sourced counter records could trigger an unrecovered panic and terminate the server process. Some malformed MQTT records could remain in storage and cause a further failure when read after restart. Exposure depends on access to the affected internal subjects or source configuration.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.12.14, v2.14.4 and v2.15.0. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-hwrp-2926-g93m>
